mnemonic.meaning: NICK, CORY (にっこり): Nick looks at Cory and smiles sweetly.

examples.ja: 赤ちゃんがにっこり笑った。
examples.en: The baby smiled sweetly.

items.note: A broad, friendly smile. にこにこ = smiling continuously.

mnemonic.meaning: It has (有) an effect (効). Valid, effective.
mnemonic.reading: YOU, COKE (ゆうこう): your Coke coupon is still valid!

examples.ja: このチケットは今月まで有効だ。
examples.en: This ticket is valid until this month.

items.note: 有効期限 = expiry date. 無効 = invalid.

mnemonic.meaning: 班 is 王 (jewel) split by a knife into two groups. A squad, a team.
mnemonic.reading: HAN (はん) Solo leads the squad.

examples.ja: 五人ずつの班に分かれた。
examples.en: We split into groups of five.

items.note: Small teams at school or work.

mnemonic.meaning: 別 is separate: two people go separate ways. A parting, a farewell.
mnemonic.reading: WACKA, RAY (わかれ): Ray waves goodbye. Farewell!

examples.ja: 別れの時が来た。
examples.en: The time to say goodbye has come.

items.note: 別れ話 = a breakup talk. Same reading as 分かれ (branch).

mnemonic.meaning: The topic (題) assigned (課) to you. A task, an assignment.
mnemonic.reading: CAR DIE (かだい): your assignment: fix the car before it dies.

examples.ja: 夏休みの課題がまだ終わらない。
examples.en: I still haven't finished my summer homework.

items.note: Homework, or an issue to tackle: 今後の課題 (things to work on).

mnemonic.meaning: The lines of longitude (経) and latitude (緯): the map of how it all happened. The circumstances.
mnemonic.reading: CAY, EE (けいい): tell me the details: how did you end up on that cay?

examples.ja: 事件の経緯を説明してください。
examples.en: Please explain how the incident came about.

items.note: Also longitude and latitude. いきさつ is the softer reading.

mnemonic.meaning: 哀 has 口 (mouth) inside 衣 (clothes): crying into your sleeve. Pitiful, sad.
mnemonic.reading: AH, WARE (あわれ): "Ah, where is my dog?" the pitiful boy cries.

examples.ja: 雨にぬれた子猫が哀れだった。
examples.en: The rain-soaked kitten was pitiful.

items.note: Literary. もののあはれ is a classic aesthetic idea.

mnemonic.meaning: A broad (博) expert gentleman (士). A doctor, a PhD.
mnemonic.reading: HACK, SAY (はかせ): the professor hacks the computer and says "I'm a doctor".

examples.ja: 彼は物理学の博士だ。
examples.en: He has a doctorate in physics.

items.note: Formal reading: はくし. Not a medical doctor (医者).

mnemonic.meaning: The warmth (温) of your body (体). Body temperature.
mnemonic.reading: TIE ON (たいおん): tie on a thermometer and check your body temperature.

examples.ja: 体温を測ったら、三十八度あった。
examples.en: I took my temperature and it was 38 degrees.

items.note: 体温計 = thermometer.

mnemonic.meaning: Eminent (偉) and big (大). Great, mighty.
mnemonic.reading: EE, DIE (いだい): the great king will never die.

examples.ja: 彼は偉大な科学者だ。
examples.en: He is a great scientist.

items.note: Formal, for people and achievements. 偉い = important, admirable.

mnemonic.meaning: 狩 has 犭 (beast): chasing a beast. Hunting.
mnemonic.reading: CARRY (かり): you carry your bow when you go hunting.

examples.ja: 昔の人は狩りをして暮らしていた。
examples.en: People long ago lived by hunting.

items.note: Also picking: いちご狩り (strawberry picking), 紅葉狩り (autumn leaf viewing).

mnemonic.meaning: "WAGA, MAMA (わがまま)!" the spoiled kid wags his finger at mama. So selfish.

examples.ja: わがままを言わないで。
examples.en: Don't be so selfish.

items.note: Kanji: 我が儘.

mnemonic.meaning: Have (有) the advantage (利). Advantageous, favourable.
mnemonic.reading: YOU REE (ゆうり): you really have the advantage.

examples.ja: 経験があると就職に有利だ。
examples.en: Experience gives you an edge when job-hunting.

items.note: Opposite: 不利 (ふり, Level 12).

mnemonic.meaning: 決 is decide: something that was decided. A rule.
mnemonic.reading: KEY, MARRY (きまり): the rule is you get a key when you marry.

examples.ja: 学校の決まりを守りましょう。
examples.en: Let's follow the school rules.

items.note: Everyday word for rules. お決まりの = the usual. 決まりが悪い = embarrassed.

mnemonic.meaning: The time (間) your hands (手) spend on it. Time and effort, trouble.
mnemonic.reading: TEH, MA (てま): sorry for the trouble, Ma.

examples.ja: この料理は手間がかかる。
examples.en: This dish takes a lot of work.

items.note: お手間をとらせました = sorry to take your time.

mnemonic.meaning: Not (不) an advantage (利). A disadvantage.
mnemonic.reading: FOO, REE (ふり): the foo dog is at a disadvantage. Same sound as 振り (pretence).

examples.ja: 雨の日の試合は私たちに不利だ。
examples.en: A match on a rainy day is to our disadvantage.

items.note: Opposite of 有利 (Level 10).

mnemonic.meaning: 嗅 has 口 (mouth/nose) + 臭 (smell): to sniff a smell.
mnemonic.reading: KA, GOO (かぐ): you smell the goo and say "ka!"

examples.ja: 犬が地面の匂いを嗅いでいる。
examples.en: The dog is sniffing the ground.

items.note: You do the smelling. Something that gives off a smell is 匂う / 臭う.

mnemonic.meaning: 陰 has 阝 (hill) + 今 (now) + 云 (cloud): the shade behind a hill when a cloud passes.
mnemonic.reading: CAGE (かげ): the bird hides in the shade behind the cage.

examples.ja: 木の陰で休んだ。
examples.en: I rested in the shade of a tree.

items.note: 陰 = shade, a hidden place. 影 = a cast shadow or silhouette. 陰で = behind someone's back.

mnemonic.meaning: 説 has 言 (words): words that explain. A theory, an opinion.
mnemonic.reading: SET, SUE (せつ): set Sue straight. Her theory is wrong.

examples.ja: この現象にはいくつかの説がある。
examples.en: There are several theories about this phenomenon.

items.note: 一説によると = according to one theory.

mnemonic.meaning: 職 has 耳 (ear): you listen to the boss's orders. A job.
mnemonic.reading: SHOCK (しょく): you're shocked: you got the job!

examples.ja: 彼は先月、職を失った。
examples.en: He lost his job last month.

items.note: 職 is formal. 仕事 is everyday. 職業 = occupation, 就職 = getting a job.

mnemonic.meaning: Your mind (意) stands its ground (地). Stubbornness, pride.
mnemonic.reading: EE, GEE (いじ)! "Gee, he's so stubborn."

examples.ja: 意地を張らないで、謝りなさい。
examples.en: Don't be stubborn. Just apologise.

items.note: 意地を張る = to be stubborn. 意地悪 = mean, spiteful.

mnemonic.meaning: People reside (居) on the lawn (芝) to watch a play. A drama, an act.
mnemonic.reading: SHE BUY (しばい): she buys tickets for the play.

examples.ja: 昨日、友達と芝居を見に行った。
examples.en: I went to see a play with a friend yesterday.

items.note: Also pretending: それは芝居だ (that's an act).

mnemonic.meaning: 群 has 羊 (sheep): sheep together. A herd, a flock.
mnemonic.reading: GOON (ぐん): a group of goons.

examples.ja: 彼の成績はクラスでも群を抜いている。
examples.en: His grades stand out even in his class.

items.note: On its own it's usually 群れ (むれ, a flock or herd). ぐん appears in 群を抜く (to stand out from the rest) and compounds like 群衆 (crowd).

mnemonic.meaning: 振 is shake, wave: a swing of the arm. Or you just pretend: a pretence.
mnemonic.reading: FOO, REE (ふり): you pretend to swing the foo stick.

examples.ja: 彼は聞こえない振りをした。
examples.en: He pretended not to hear.

items.note: 〜振りをする = pretend (often in kana: ふり). 久しぶり uses ぶり: after a long time.

mnemonic.meaning: High (高) and fast (速). High speed, the expressway.
mnemonic.reading: COAT SOCK (こうそく): at high speed your coat and sock fly off on the expressway.

examples.ja: 高速で一時間ほど走った。
examples.en: We drove about an hour on the expressway.

items.note: Short for 高速道路 (expressway). 高速バス = highway bus.

mnemonic.meaning: 瓶 has 瓦 (pottery): a pottery jar. A bottle.
mnemonic.reading: BIN (びん): you throw your empty bottle into the bin.

examples.ja: 空き瓶を捨てた。
examples.en: I threw away the empty bottles.

items.note: Glass bottles. Plastic ones are ペットボトル.

mnemonic.meaning: 段 is step, stage: a step, a level.
mnemonic.reading: DAN (だん) climbs the stairs one step at a time.

examples.ja: 一段ずつ階段を上った。
examples.en: I climbed the stairs one step at a time.

items.note: Also ranks in martial arts and go: 三段 (third dan).

mnemonic.meaning: 劣 is 少 (few) + 力 (power): less power. To be inferior.
mnemonic.reading: OH, TORU (おとる): Oh, Toru is worse at soccer.

examples.ja: 品質では他社に劣らない。
examples.en: In quality we're as good as the other companies.

items.note: Often 〜に劣らない = not inferior to. 優れる is the opposite.

mnemonic.meaning: 泡 has 氵 (water) + 包 (wrap): water wrapped around air. A bubble.
mnemonic.reading: AWWA (あわ): "Aww, a bubble!" the baby says. Foam everywhere.

examples.ja: ビールの泡がこぼれた。
examples.en: The beer foam spilled over.

items.note: 泡を食う = to be flustered.

mnemonic.meaning: 紐 has 糸 (thread): a string, a cord.
mnemonic.reading: HE, MO' (ひも): he wants more string.

examples.ja: 靴の紐がほどけているよ。
examples.en: Your shoelace is untied.

items.note: ひも is also slang for a man who lives off his partner.
